name_reason: Name is compliant and descriptive: data_fd2_battle_ prefix (battle core table), descriptor weapon_attack_anim_pattern_script_pool accurately captures the per-weapon attack-hit animation script pool. Suffix _84b is the real array dimension (pool is exactly 84 bytes: 0x619FD - 0x619A9 = 0x54 = 84, also matches the C declaration [84]); it is NOT a Ghidra address residue (the address is 0x619A9, not 0x54/84). Size suffix legitimately reflects the data type/shape per project naming convention.
purpose: Packed pool of per-weapon-type attack-hit animation scripts; each script drives the hit-sprite + SFX sequence played when a weapon's attack lands. Records are shared across weapon types via the preceding 21-entry pointer table.
logic_summary: 84-byte byte array holding 6 variable-length records packed back-to-back. Indirected by data_fd2_battle_weapon_attack_anim_pattern_ptr_table_21 @ 0x61955 (21 dword entries indexed by weapon attack-pattern id 0..20; each entry = &pool[offset], several slots share the same record). Sole table reader: fd2_get_attack_anim_pattern_for_weapon @ 0x4E52D (asm: SHL EBX,2; MOV EAX,[EBX+0x61955]; returns table[weapon_type]). Pool reader: fd2_animate_attack_hit_sequence @ 0x1E98C, which treats the returned pointer p as: step_count=p[0]; for s in 0..step_count: sprite_id=p[2*s+1], sfx_id=p[2*s+2] (sfx_id 0xFF means no sound). Record length = 1 + 2*step_count. Record start offsets in pool: +0,+13,+26 (6 steps each); +39,+56 (8 steps each); +73 (5 steps). Bytes verified byte-identical between Ghidra memory @ 0x619A9 and the C source array.
datatype: const uint8[84] (packed variable-length records; each record = { uint8 step_count, (uint8 sprite_id, uint8 sfx_id) * step_count })
element_semantics: Per record: byte[0]=step_count (number of animation steps); then step_count pairs of (sprite_id, sfx_id). sprite_id selects the hit/swing sprite drawn at the defender for that step; sfx_id selects the sound effect for that step, with 0xFF meaning silent for that step. Records are packed contiguously; multiple ptr-table slots may alias the same record offset.
notes: src comment block (btltab3.c lines 536-562) and per-record inline comments are already accurate, precise, ASCII-only, and match the Ghidra disassembly/decompilation; left unchanged (comment_verdict=keep), so src/table/btltab3.c has no content edits. Ghidra data plate at 0x619A9 was empty (null); created a concise plate (PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline) documenting symbol/size/const, the indirecting ptr table @ 0x61955, the record format read by fd2_animate_attack_hit_sequence @ 0x1E98C, and record offsets -- consistent with the src conclusion. const confirmed: get_xrefs_to on pool entry points (0x619A9/B6/C3/E1/F2) shows only address-of DATA refs from the ptr table range 0x61955-0x619A5; no writers anywhere. _84b suffix kept (real dimension, not address residue). No logic/equivalence issues found.
